correctness.rationale: For arbitrary nonnegative gaps, the two-marker lemma proves the four-piece upper bound. Exact two-piece conditions follow by exhausting the one-count allocations of two palindromes; the four-piece lower bound follows from the impossibility of marked palindromic prefixes or suffixes and unequal inner gaps. Explicit three-piece decompositions finish all remaining cases. Gap enumeration gives the rational generating function and its pole at one gives density one-sixth. A standalone dynamic program independently checked 14641 gap quadruples; direct position-based word enumeration and rational-series expansion matched for lengths 3-28. The unrestricted result depends on proof, not finite tests.

evidence: Palindromic length is also minimum number of palindrome factors or membership in a bounded product of palindrome languages; the present result solves this exact membership for all three-one binary words.
Frid, Puzynina and Zamboni 2012 study unbounded palindromic lengths of factors in infinite words, without this four-gap finite classification.

originality.rationale: A new exact four-tier formula on all nonnegative zero gaps and a rational generating function with asymptotic density 1/6 distinguish the result from global worst-case palindromic-length estimates and qualitative infinite-word factorization results. Checked primary texts and topical searches did not identify an explicit covering parametric classification; older or unindexed equivalents remain a real risk.

Earlier hardcopy versions of relevant cited papers may have publication dates preceding their verified arXiv versions; the archival cutoff is unaffected.

value.rationale: The family of all binary strings with exactly three occurrences of one symbol is a natural first sparse family capable of needing four palindrome factors. The theorem classifies every parameter value including equality boundaries, determines the complete extremal sublanguage with a rational generating series, identifies the first length-eight examples, and shows a limiting exact proportion of one sixth; none of these is a routine relabeling of a global maximum table. The result offers a sharp benchmark for minimum palindromic factorization in sparse inputs without claiming a general algorithm.
